# Overview

The firefly transfection-efficiency control, in **both orientations**:

```
C-terminal firefly   mCherry - HA - (GGGGS)x3 - P2A - firefly
N-terminal firefly   firefly - (GGGGS)x3 - P2A - mCherry - HA
```

Each is one ORF, measured as one CDS. The notebook answers the same two
questions for both - **how long** and **where does GC3 sit** - and places them
together on the two panels `01_` uses, with nothing else on the figure.

**A 1xHA tag sits at mCherry's own C terminus in both**, which puts it in a
different place in the ORF each time: immediately before the GS linker when
mCherry leads, and at the very end of the construct when mCherry trails. It
follows mCherry rather than a fixed position, so the builder works from an
ordered part layout rather than an upstream/downstream pair.

**The two orientations are the same length, exactly, and that is structural
rather than a coincidence.** Both constructs hold the same five parts; only
their order differs. Every part's terminal stop is stripped and a single `TAA`
is appended to the finished ORF, so neither orientation can gain or lose a
codon relative to the other. Both are 2,613 nt ordered. A length comparison
between them is therefore perfectly controlled, and on the length panel the two
reference lines fall on top of each other - drawn with different linetypes so
neither is hidden.

**Composition as supplied is nowhere near typical.** mCherry is GC3 97.0% and
the GS linker's naive encoding is GC3 100%, putting either assembled construct
near **GC3 83.5%** against an expressed-transcriptome median of 57.3%. So
mCherry, the GS linker and firefly are **recoded synonymously** onto the 231
composition in each orientation. The protein is unchanged at every position and
the length cannot change, because synonymous recoding never does.

**P2A is the one part held fixed in both.** It works by ribosomal skipping of
its own Gly-Pro bond, so its sequence is the mechanism rather than a carrier of
composition.

**Assembly rules, each forced rather than chosen:**

1. **Every part's terminal stop is stripped.** A stop 5' of P2A would end
   translation before the downstream protein ever appears, and mCherry can no
   longer be 3'-most on its own now that HA follows it. Both mCherry and
   firefly are supplied with one, so both lose it.
2. **A single `TAA` is appended to the finished ORF**, at the end of the full
   CDS and nowhere else. Applying one rule to both orientations is what makes
   their lengths identical by construction rather than by arithmetic accident.
3. **The (GGGGS)x3 linker always sits between the upstream part and P2A**, in
   both orientations, as it does in the HiBiT ladder: P2A leaves its own
   18-residue tail fused to whatever is upstream, and a flexible spacer keeps
   that tail off the upstream protein's fold. The spreadsheet has no GS linker
   row, so its DNA is designed here.
4. **No EcoRI constraint.** The eGFP ladder pins the `GAATTC` count because its
   Waldo linker carries the one intended site; these constructs have no Waldo
   linker, so there is no site to protect and the count is reported rather than
   constrained.

**Lengths are reported stop-free**, matching how the gene CDS lengths on the
panels are measured. The ordered insert is 3 nt longer than the plotted number.

# 1. Load Libraries

```{r load_libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(readxl)
library(GenomicFeatures)
library(BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38)
library(Biostrings)

source(here("code", "cds_reporter_design", "reporter_helpers.R"))
source(here("code", "cds_reporter_design", "recoder.R"))
```

```{r params_chunk}
lfc_cutoff  <- 0.5
padj_cutoff <- 0.05

stopifnot(
  "min_codon_prop must be in (0, 1/6)" =
    params$min_codon_prop > 0 && params$min_codon_prop < 1 / 6,
  "max_homopolymer must be at least 4" = params$max_homopolymer >= 4,
  "gs_repeats must be at least 2 for the repeat checks to mean anything" =
    params$gs_repeats >= 2,
  "gs_max_repeat must be below the 15 nt GGGGS unit length" =
    params$gs_max_repeat >= 3 && params$gs_max_repeat < 15,
  "gs_max_homopolymer must not exceed the construct-wide cap" =
    params$gs_max_homopolymer >= 4 &&
    params$gs_max_homopolymer <= params$max_homopolymer
)
```

# 2. Import and Verify the Parts

```{r read_parts}
parts_xlsx <- here("accessories", "cds seq.xlsx")
stopifnot("accessories/cds seq.xlsx not found" = file.exists(parts_xlsx))

parts_tbl <- read_excel(parts_xlsx)
names(parts_tbl)[1] <- "construct"

parts <- parts_tbl %>%
  filter(!is.na(construct), !is.na(cds)) %>%
  transmute(part = tolower(str_trim(construct)),
            seq  = toupper(gsub("\\s", "", cds)))
stopifnot("Duplicate part names in cds seq.xlsx" = !any(duplicated(parts$part)))
pseq <- setNames(parts$seq, parts$part)

needed <- c("mcherry", "p2a", "firefly", "ha")
stopifnot(
  "A required part is missing from cds seq.xlsx" = all(needed %in% names(pseq)),
  "A part contains non-ACGT characters" = all(!grepl("[^ACGT]", pseq[needed])),
  "A part is not divisible by 3" = all(nchar(pseq[needed]) %% 3 == 0)
)

mcherry_raw <- pseq[["mcherry"]]
p2a         <- pseq[["p2a"]]
firefly_raw <- pseq[["firefly"]]
ha          <- pseq[["ha"]]

aa_of <- function(s) as.character(translate(DNAString(s)))
rc_aa <- function(s) as.character(translate(reverseComplement(DNAString(s))))

P2A_AA <- "ATNFSLLKQAGDVEENPGP"
HA_AA  <- "YPYDVPDYA"

stopifnot(
  "p2a does not encode the expected 19-aa P2A peptide" = aa_of(p2a) == P2A_AA,
  # 1xHA. The spreadsheet also carries `3x ha` (29 aa) and a 1-codon `ha
  # linker`; this is the bare 9-residue epitope, asserted by peptide so the
  # wrong row cannot be picked up silently.
  "ha does not encode the 9-residue HA epitope YPYDVPDYA" = aa_of(ha) == HA_AA,
  "ha is not 27 nt" = nchar(ha) == 27,
  "ha carries a stop codon" = !any(codon_split(ha) %in% STOP_CODONS),
  "Both orientations encode HA: the check is not discriminative" =
    rc_aa(ha) != HA_AA,
  # Both parts must be able to serve as the ORF's initiator, since either can
  # be the upstream one.
  "mcherry does not start with ATG" = substr(mcherry_raw, 1, 3) == "ATG",
  "firefly does not start with ATG" = substr(firefly_raw, 1, 3) == "ATG",
  # Orientation: a sequence can be in frame, the right length and still
  # backwards, so each check is paired with the assertion that the reverse
  # complement does NOT encode the same peptide.
  "Both orientations encode P2A: the check is not discriminative" =
    rc_aa(p2a) != P2A_AA,
  "Both orientations encode mCherry: the check is not discriminative" =
    rc_aa(mcherry_raw) != aa_of(mcherry_raw),
  "Both orientations encode firefly: the check is not discriminative" =
    rc_aa(firefly_raw) != aa_of(firefly_raw)
)
```

```{r verify_stops}
# Rules 1 and 2 are only well defined if BOTH parts carry a terminal stop: that
# is what makes the two orientations the same length, since exactly one stop is
# stripped whichever way round they go. Asserted rather than assumed.
mch_cv <- codon_split(mcherry_raw)
ff_cv  <- codon_split(firefly_raw)

stopifnot(
  "mCherry does not end in a stop codon" = tail(mch_cv, 1) %in% STOP_CODONS,
  "mCherry has an internal stop codon" =
    !any(head(mch_cv, -1) %in% STOP_CODONS),
  "firefly does not end in a stop codon" = tail(ff_cv, 1) %in% STOP_CODONS,
  "firefly has an internal stop codon" =
    !any(head(ff_cv, -1) %in% STOP_CODONS),
  "P2A carries a stop codon" = !any(codon_split(p2a) %in% STOP_CODONS)
)
cat(sprintf("mCherry %d nt, terminal %s | firefly %d nt, terminal %s\n",
            nchar(mcherry_raw), tail(mch_cv, 1),
            nchar(firefly_raw), tail(ff_cv, 1)))
```

**The firefly sequence is checked against the copy already in the repo.**
`code/predictive_modeling/62_cds_length_gc_hypoxia_promotes.Rmd` carries the
lab's luc2P inline. Parsing it out of that file and asserting the spreadsheet
matches is the project's standing rule - import and verify, never transcribe -
and here it is also the check that catches the **PEST-less** version of the same
gene, which is a prefix of this one and would otherwise pass every length, frame
and start-codon test.

```{r verify_firefly_against_repo}
nb62 <- readLines(here("code", "predictive_modeling",
                       "62_cds_length_gc_hypoxia_promotes.Rmd"), warn = FALSE)
ff_line <- grep("^ff_seq <- toupper", nb62)
stopifnot("Could not find ff_seq in notebook 62_" = length(ff_line) == 1)
ff_repo <- toupper(sub('.*toupper\\("([acgtACGT]+)".*', "\\1", nb62[ff_line]))

stopifnot(
  "The spreadsheet firefly does not match the luc2P sequence in notebook 62_" =
    identical(firefly_raw, ff_repo),
  "Parsed repo sequence is implausibly short: the regex did not capture it" =
    nchar(ff_repo) > 1000
)
cat(sprintf("firefly verified against 62_: %d nt, bit-identical\n",
            nchar(ff_repo)))

PEST_AA <- "NSHGFPPEVEEQAAGTLPMSCAQESGMDRHPAACASARINV"
ff_aa_full <- aa_of(substr(firefly_raw, 1, nchar(firefly_raw) - 3))
stopifnot(
  "firefly does not carry the 41-aa PEST degron at its C terminus" =
    endsWith(ff_aa_full, PEST_AA)
)
cat(sprintf("firefly is luc2P: %d aa = luc2 %d aa + the %d-aa PEST degron\n",
            nchar(ff_aa_full), nchar(ff_aa_full) - nchar(PEST_AA),
            nchar(PEST_AA)))
```

# 3. MDA-MB-231 Background and the GC3 Target

Same derivation as `01_` and `08_`: the target is computed from the transcript
set the panels plot, never typed in.

```{r load_promotes}
te_hyp <- read_csv(
  here("output", "translation_categories_si3d_vs_sictrl_hypoxia_1hr.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE)

# Direction check. These files hold the sictrl_vs_si3d coefficient despite the
# filename stating the ratio the other way round, so positive te_lfc = eIF3d
# promotes. EIF3D's own rna_lfc must be strongly positive.
eif3d_rna <- te_hyp %>% filter(symbol == "EIF3D") %>% pull(rna_lfc)
stopifnot("EIF3D rna_lfc is not strongly positive: contrast direction may be flipped" =
            length(eif3d_rna) == 1 && eif3d_rna > 2)
cat("Direction check - EIF3D rna_lfc:", round(eif3d_rna, 2), "\n")

promotes <- te_hyp %>%
  filter(te_lfc > lfc_cutoff, te_padj < padj_cutoff) %>%
  mutate(gene_id_clean = sub("\\..*", "", gene_id))
stopifnot("Expected 1604 eIF3d hypoxia-promoted genes" = nrow(promotes) == 1604)
```

```{r transcripts}
fm <- readRDS(here("output", "predictive_modeling",
                   "feature_matrix_external_stability.rds"))
tx_all      <- fm %>% dplyr::select(transcript_id_clean, gene_id_clean, symbol)
tx_promotes <- tx_all %>% filter(gene_id_clean %in% promotes$gene_id_clean)

missing_gene_ids <- promotes$gene_id_clean[
  !promotes$gene_id_clean %in% tx_all$gene_id_clean]

tx_map <- read_tsv(
  here("accessories", "human", "tx2gene_hs_dm_v49_r111.tsv.gz"),
  col_names = c("transcript_id", "gene_id"), col_types = "cc") %>%
  filter(str_starts(transcript_id, "ENST")) %>%
  transmute(transcript_id_clean = sub("\\..*", "", transcript_id),
            gene_id_clean       = sub("\\..*", "", gene_id))

hyp_samples <- c("NM2025_0094", "NM2025_0095", "NM2025_0096")
hyp_files   <- setNames(
  file.path(here("2025_MDAcells_riboseq", "salmon"), hyp_samples, "quant.sf.gz"),
  hyp_samples)
stopifnot("Hypoxia siCTRL quant files missing" = all(file.exists(hyp_files)))

extra_tx_df <- map_dfr(names(hyp_files), function(s) {
  read_tsv(hyp_files[[s]], col_types = "cdddd",
           col_names = c("Name", "Length", "EffectiveLength", "TPM", "NumReads"),
           skip = 1) %>% dplyr::select(Name, TPM)
}) %>%
  group_by(Name) %>% summarise(mean_tpm = mean(TPM), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(transcript_id_clean = sub("\\..*", "", Name)) %>%
  inner_join(tx_map, by = "transcript_id_clean") %>%
  filter(gene_id_clean %in% missing_gene_ids, mean_tpm > 0) %>%
  group_by(gene_id_clean) %>%
  dplyr::slice_max(mean_tpm, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(promotes %>% dplyr::select(gene_id_clean, symbol) %>% distinct(),
            by = "gene_id_clean") %>%
  dplyr::select(transcript_id_clean, gene_id_clean, symbol)

tx_promotes <- bind_rows(tx_promotes, extra_tx_df)
```

```{r build_metrics}
cds_seqs    <- build_cds_seqs(here("accessories", "human",
                                   "txdb.gencode49.sqlite"))
cds_int     <- DNAStringSet(trim_internal(as.character(cds_seqs)))
names(cds_int) <- names(cds_seqs)

cds_nostop  <- subseq(cds_seqs, start = 1L,
                      end = BiocGenerics::width(cds_seqs) - 3L)
metrics_all <- tibble(
  transcript_id_clean = names(cds_seqs),
  cds_length = BiocGenerics::width(cds_nostop),
  gc_pct  = as.numeric(letterFrequency(cds_nostop, letters = "GC",
                                       as.prob = TRUE)) * 100,
  gc3_pct = sapply(as.character(cds_int), compute_gc3_pct, USE.NAMES = FALSE)
)

expressed <- tx_all %>%
  inner_join(metrics_all, by = "transcript_id_clean") %>% filter(cds_length > 0)
promoted <- tx_promotes %>%
  inner_join(metrics_all, by = "transcript_id_clean") %>% filter(cds_length > 0)

stopifnot(
  "GC3% out of range" = all(between(expressed$gc3_pct, 0, 100)),
  "GC3 median not in expected range [40, 65]" =
    between(median(expressed$gc3_pct), 40, 65)
)
actb <- expressed %>% filter(symbol == "ACTB") %>% dplyr::slice(1)
stopifnot("ACTB CDS GC% outside expected 50-70%" = between(actb$gc_pct, 50, 70))

TARGET_GC3 <- median(expressed$gc3_pct)
cat(sprintf("Expressed n = %s, GC3 target %.2f%%, median length %s nt\n",
            fmt_n(nrow(expressed)), TARGET_GC3,
            fmt_n(median(expressed$cds_length))))
cat(sprintf("Promoted  n = %s, median GC3 %.1f%%, median length %s nt\n",
            fmt_n(nrow(promoted)), median(promoted$gc3_pct),
            fmt_n(median(promoted$cds_length))))
```

# 4. Codon Usage of the Expressed Transcriptome

```{r codon_usage}
GEN <- GENETIC_CODE
AA  <- setNames(as.character(GEN), names(GEN))
stopifnot("Codon-to-amino-acid lookup lost its names" =
            identical(names(AA), names(GEN)))
sense <- names(GEN)[AA != "*"]

expr_seqs <- cds_int[names(cds_int) %in% expressed$transcript_id_clean]
cf <- trinucleotideFrequency(expr_seqs, step = 3)
stopifnot("trinucleotideFrequency lost its codon column names" =
            !is.null(colnames(cf)) && all(names(GEN) %in% colnames(cf)))

usage <- tibble(codon = colnames(cf), count = colSums(cf)) %>%
  filter(AA[codon] != "*") %>%
  mutate(aa = AA[codon]) %>%
  group_by(aa) %>% mutate(prop = count / sum(count)) %>% ungroup()
stopifnot(
  "Synonymous proportions do not sum to 1 within every amino acid" =
    all(abs((usage %>% group_by(aa) %>% summarise(s = sum(prop)))$s - 1) < 1e-9),
  "A sense codon is missing from the usage table" = setequal(usage$codon, sense)
)
leu <- usage %>% filter(aa == "L") %>% dplyr::slice_max(prop, n = 1)
stopifnot("CTG is not the most-used Leu codon: usage table may be misaligned" =
            leu$codon == "CTG")

USE   <- setNames(usage$prop, usage$codon)
BASES <- c("A", "C", "G", "T")

pick_list <- function(cods) {
  keep <- cods[USE[cods] >= params$min_codon_prop]
  if (!length(keep)) cods[which.max(USE[cods])] else keep
}
MENU <- map(split(sense, AA[sense]), function(cods) {
  by_base <- map(setNames(BASES, BASES), ~ cods[str_sub(cods, 3, 3) == .x])
  map(by_base[lengths(by_base) > 0], pick_list)
})
```

```{r base_ratios}
b3_col  <- str_sub(colnames(cf), 3, 3)
tx_n3   <- sapply(setNames(BASES, BASES),
                  function(b) rowSums(cf[, b3_col == b, drop = FALSE]))
tx_pct3 <- 100 * tx_n3 / rowSums(tx_n3)
med3 <- apply(tx_pct3, 2, median)
R_G <- med3[["G"]] / (med3[["G"]] + med3[["C"]])
R_A <- med3[["A"]] / (med3[["A"]] + med3[["T"]])
stopifnot(
  "Third-base split ratios are out of range" =
    between(R_G, 0, 1) && between(R_A, 0, 1),
  "Split ratios and the GC3 target disagree: they are not the same statistic" =
    abs((med3[["G"]] + med3[["C"]]) / sum(med3) * 100 - TARGET_GC3) < 1
)
cat(sprintf("G:(G+C) = %.3f   A:(A+T) = %.3f\n", R_G, R_A))
```

# 5. The GS Linker

```{r gs_linker}
GS_UNIT_AA <- "GGGGS"
GS_UNIT_NT <- 3L * nchar(GS_UNIT_AA)
gs_aa      <- strrep(GS_UNIT_AA, params$gs_repeats)

# The linker's PRE-recode state is the naive encoding - the most-used codon per
# residue in this same 231 table - which is what a synthesis vendor's optimizer
# returns and is the exact tandem repeat the recoding has to break.
gs_naive <- naive_encoding(gs_aa, usage)
gs_cv    <- codon_split(gs_naive)
n_gs     <- length(gs_cv)

gs_units <- function(linker)
  substring(linker,
            seq(1L, by = GS_UNIT_NT, length.out = params$gs_repeats),
            seq(GS_UNIT_NT, by = GS_UNIT_NT, length.out = params$gs_repeats))
longest_homopolymer <- function(s)
  max(nchar(str_extract_all(s, "(A+|C+|G+|T+)")[[1]]))

stopifnot(
  "The naive GS linker does not encode the GGGGS repeat" =
    aa_of(gs_naive) == gs_aa,
  "The naive GS linker is not a tandem repeat: the repeat constraint has no motivation" =
    length(unique(gs_units(gs_naive))) == 1L
)

# Glycine's only G-ending codon is GGG, and inside a polyglycine run it is
# always followed by another GG, so picking it puts a 5 nt G run in the linker.
# The construct-wide menu cannot say "not here", so the linker's glycines give
# up G and the G-enders the target needs go elsewhere.
gs_menus <- map(MENU[AA[gs_cv]], function(m)
  if (identical(m[["G"]], "GGG")) m[names(m) != "G"] else m)
stopifnot("The GS menu restriction did not remove GGG" =
            !any(map_lgl(gs_menus, ~ "GGG" %in% unlist(.x))))
cat("Naive GS linker:", gs_naive, "| GC3",
    round(compute_gc3_pct(gs_naive), 1), "%\n")
```

# 6. Build Both Orientations

One builder, driven by an **ordered part layout** rather than an
upstream/downstream pair. HA follows mCherry wherever mCherry sits, so the two
orientations are not mirror images of one another and a builder phrased as
"upstream part, linker, P2A, downstream part" cannot express them both.

Every sense codon except the initiator and P2A's nineteen is free, and they are
drawn as **one assignment** rather than block by block, because the third-base
target is a count over the whole construct and splitting it between parts would
need an arbitrary allocation. `assign_third_bases` reads amino acids off a plain
vector and never looks at position, so the free codons do not have to be
contiguous - which is what lets HA, sitting in a different place in each
orientation, be handled without a special case.

```{r builder}
R <- make_recoder(TARGET_GC3, R_G, R_A, MENU, USE, AA, params$max_homopolymer)

strip_terminal_stop <- function(s)
  if (tail(codon_split(s), 1) %in% STOP_CODONS) substr(s, 1, nchar(s) - 3) else s

P2A_PART <- "P2A (fixed)"
GS_PART  <- sprintf("GS linker (%dxGGGGS)", params$gs_repeats)
ORF_STOP <- "TAA"

# Sense forms of every part: stops stripped, so the ORF gains exactly one
# terminator at the very end regardless of how the parts are ordered.
sense_parts <- list(
  "mCherry"       = strip_terminal_stop(mcherry_raw),
  "HA (1x)"       = ha,
  GS_PART         = gs_naive,
  P2A_PART        = p2a,
  "firefly luc2P" = strip_terminal_stop(firefly_raw))
names(sense_parts)[3:4] <- c(GS_PART, P2A_PART)

stopifnot(
  "A sense part still carries a stop codon" =
    !any(map_lgl(sense_parts, ~ any(codon_split(.x) %in% STOP_CODONS)))
)

# layout: the part names in construct order.
build_orientation <- function(label, layout, seed = params$seed) {
  stopifnot(
    "A layout names a part that does not exist" =
      all(layout %in% names(sense_parts)),
    "A layout does not use every part exactly once" =
      setequal(layout, names(sense_parts)) && !any(duplicated(layout))
  )

  cvs    <- map(sense_parts[layout], codon_split)
  ends   <- cumsum(lengths(cvs))
  starts <- ends - lengths(cvs) + 1L
  all_cv <- unlist(cvs, use.names = FALSE)

  idx_of <- function(nm) {
    i <- match(nm, layout); starts[i]:ends[i]
  }

  # Fixed: the construct's initiator (position 1, whichever part leads) and all
  # of P2A. Everything else is free.
  fixed_idx <- c(1L, idx_of(P2A_PART))
  free_idx  <- setdiff(seq_along(all_cv), fixed_idx)
  free_cv   <- all_cv[free_idx]

  # Per-position menus. The GS linker's glycines give up GGG - inside a
  # polyglycine run it is always followed by another GG, which would put a 5 nt
  # G run in the linker - so those positions carry a narrowed menu that a menu
  # keyed by amino acid cannot express.
  gs_global  <- idx_of(GS_PART)
  free_menus <- map(seq_along(free_idx), function(k) {
    g <- free_idx[k]
    m <- MENU[[AA[[all_cv[g]]]]]
    if (g %in% gs_global && identical(m[["G"]], "GGG")) m[names(m) != "G"] else m
  })
  gs_in_block <- which(free_idx %in% gs_global)
  stopifnot(
    "The GS linker is not entirely free" = length(gs_in_block) == n_gs,
    "The GS menu restriction did not remove GGG" =
      !any(map_lgl(free_menus[gs_in_block], ~ "GGG" %in% unlist(.x)))
  )

  assemble <- function(b) { out <- all_cv; out[free_idx] <- b; out }

  gs_ok <- function(block) {
    linker <- paste0(block[gs_in_block], collapse = "")
    anyDuplicated(gs_units(linker)) == 0L &&
      max_internal_repeat(linker) <= params$gs_max_repeat &&
      longest_homopolymer(linker) <= params$gs_max_homopolymer
  }

  set.seed(seed)
  need  <- R$block_needs(length(free_cv), all_cv[fixed_idx])
  drawn <- R$draw_clean_block(
    free_cv, need, assemble = assemble,
    n_linkers = NA,            # no EcoRI requirement in these constructs
    extra_ok = gs_ok, menus = free_menus, max_try = 5000)

  recoded_cv    <- assemble(drawn$block)
  recoded_sense <- paste0(recoded_cv, collapse = "")

  cat(sprintf("%-18s %s | free %d of %d codons; clean draw %d\n",
              label, paste(layout, collapse = " - "),
              length(free_cv), length(all_cv), drawn$tries))

  list(
    label = label, layout = layout,
    original_sense = paste0(unlist(sense_parts[layout]), collapse = ""),
    sense = recoded_sense,
    full  = paste0(recoded_sense, ORF_STOP),
    parts = tibble(
      part   = layout,
      before = map_chr(layout, ~ sense_parts[[.x]]),
      after  = map_chr(layout, ~ paste0(recoded_cv[idx_of(.x)], collapse = ""))),
    p2a_at = idx_of(P2A_PART)
  )
}

builds <- list(
  build_orientation("C-terminal firefly",
                    c("mCherry", "HA (1x)", GS_PART, P2A_PART, "firefly luc2P")),
  build_orientation("N-terminal firefly",
                    c("firefly luc2P", GS_PART, P2A_PART, "mCherry", "HA (1x)"))
)
names(builds) <- map_chr(builds, "label")

construct_names <- c("C-terminal firefly" = "mCherry-HA-GS-P2A-firefly",
                     "N-terminal firefly" = "firefly-GS-P2A-mCherry-HA")
```

# 7. Validation

Checked on DNA translated independently rather than on the bookkeeping that
produced it, for both orientations.

```{r validate_protein}
walk(builds, function(b) {
  stopifnot(
    "Recoded ORF differs in length from the original" =
      nchar(b$sense) == nchar(b$original_sense),
    "Recoding changed the protein" =
      aa_of(b$sense) == aa_of(b$original_sense),
    "Recoded ORF lost frame" = nchar(b$full) %% 3 == 0,
    "Recoded ORF does not start with the initiator" =
      substr(b$full, 1, 3) == "ATG",
    # The terminator rule, both halves of it: exactly one stop, at the very end.
    "Recoded ORF does not end in the terminator" =
      tail(codon_split(b$full), 1) == ORF_STOP,
    "Recoded ORF carries a stop before the end - including before P2A" =
      !any(head(codon_split(b$full), -1) %in% STOP_CODONS),
    "P2A is not bit-identical in the recoded construct" =
      paste0(codon_split(b$sense)[b$p2a_at], collapse = "") == p2a,
    # Discriminative companion: the free parts must NOT be unchanged, or
    # nothing was recoded and every composition check below would still pass.
    "A free part was not recoded" =
      all((b$parts$before != b$parts$after)[b$parts$part != P2A_PART])
  )
})
cat("Both orientations: protein unchanged, P2A bit-identical, all free parts changed\n")
cat("Both ORFs carry exactly one stop codon, at the end\n")

walk(builds, function(b) {
  n_changed <- sum(codon_split(b$sense) != codon_split(b$original_sense))
  cat(sprintf("  %-18s %s aa protein; %s codons changed\n", b$label,
              fmt_n(nchar(b$sense) / 3), fmt_n(n_changed)))
})
```

**HA must sit at mCherry's own C terminus in both**, which is the point of the
layout. Checked on the protein rather than on the part order, so a layout typo
could not pass.

```{r validate_ha}
walk(builds, function(b) {
  prot    <- aa_of(b$sense)
  mch_pep <- aa_of(sense_parts[["mCherry"]])
  # The HA epitope must begin exactly where the mCherry peptide ends.
  mch_at <- str_locate(prot, fixed(mch_pep))
  stopifnot(
    "The mCherry peptide is not present in the construct" = !is.na(mch_at[1]),
    "HA does not immediately follow mCherry" =
      substr(prot, mch_at[2] + 1, mch_at[2] + nchar(HA_AA)) == HA_AA
  )
  cat(sprintf("  %-18s mCherry ends at residue %d, HA at %d-%d\n", b$label,
              mch_at[2], mch_at[2] + 1, mch_at[2] + nchar(HA_AA)))
})

# Discriminative companion: HA must appear ONCE, or a duplicated tag would
# satisfy the adjacency test above while the construct carried two epitopes.
walk(builds, function(b)
  stopifnot("HA appears more than once in the construct" =
              str_count(aa_of(b$sense), fixed(HA_AA)) == 1))
cat("HA present exactly once in each construct, immediately after mCherry\n")
```

**The two orientations must be the same length.** Every part's stop is stripped
and one terminator is appended, so the two ORFs hold the same codons in a
different order - asserted against the part arithmetic rather than observed.

```{r validate_length_match}
lens <- map_int(builds, ~ nchar(.x$sense))
expected <- sum(nchar(unlist(sense_parts)))
stopifnot(
  "The two orientations are not the same length" = length(unique(lens)) == 1,
  "Orientation lengths do not match the part arithmetic" =
    unique(lens) == expected
)
cat(sprintf("Both orientations: %s nt stop-free, %s nt ordered, identical by construction\n",
            fmt_n(unique(lens)), fmt_n(unique(lens) + 3)))

# Discriminative companion: same length must NOT mean same sequence, or the
# builder is returning one construct twice.
stopifnot("The two orientations are the same sequence" =
            builds[[1]]$sense != builds[[2]]$sense)

# Both must carry both full proteins, whichever way round they go.
mch_pep <- aa_of(sense_parts[["mCherry"]])
ff_pep  <- aa_of(sense_parts[["firefly luc2P"]])
walk(builds, function(b) {
  prot <- aa_of(b$sense)
  stopifnot(
    "Recoded construct does not contain the mCherry peptide" =
      str_detect(prot, fixed(mch_pep)),
    "Recoded construct does not contain the firefly peptide" =
      str_detect(prot, fixed(ff_pep))
  )
})
cat("Both constructs carry the full mCherry and firefly peptides\n")
```

```{r validate_motifs}
walk(builds, function(b) {
  max_run <- max(nchar(str_extract_all(b$full, "(A+|C+|G+|T+)")[[1]]))
  stopifnot("A construct carries a homopolymer longer than the cap" =
              max_run <= params$max_homopolymer)
  cat(sprintf("  %-18s longest homopolymer %d nt (cap %d) | EcoRI sites %d (before recoding %d)\n",
              b$label, max_run, params$max_homopolymer,
              str_count(b$full, fixed("GAATTC")),
              str_count(paste0(b$original_sense, ORF_STOP), fixed("GAATTC"))))
})
```

```{r validate_gs_linker}
gs_stats <- bind_rows(
  tibble(construct = "Naive (most-used codon)", seq = gs_naive),
  map_dfr(builds, ~ tibble(construct = .x$label,
                           seq = .x$parts$after[.x$parts$part == GS_PART]))) %>%
  mutate(n_units   = map_int(seq, ~ length(unique(gs_units(.x)))),
         repeat_nt = map_int(seq, max_internal_repeat),
         homo_nt   = map_int(seq, longest_homopolymer),
         gc3_pct   = map_dbl(seq, compute_gc3_pct))
print(gs_stats %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>%
        as.data.frame())

walk(builds, function(b) {
  s <- b$parts$after[b$parts$part == GS_PART]
  stopifnot(
    "A recoded GS linker changed the peptide" = aa_of(s) == gs_aa,
    "Two GGGGS units in a recoded linker are identical" =
      length(unique(gs_units(s))) == params$gs_repeats,
    "A recoded GS linker still carries a long internal repeat" =
      max_internal_repeat(s) <= params$gs_max_repeat,
    "A recoded GS linker exceeds its homopolymer cap" =
      longest_homopolymer(s) <= params$gs_max_homopolymer
  )
})
stopifnot(
  # Discriminative companions: both measures must FIRE on the naive encoding.
  "The repeat measure does not detect the naive tandem repeat" =
    max_internal_repeat(gs_naive) >= nchar(gs_naive) - GS_UNIT_NT,
  "The naive encoding passes the unit-distinctness check: not discriminative" =
    length(unique(gs_units(gs_naive))) < params$gs_repeats
)
```

```{r spot_checks}
# Biological spot-checks on proteins that must survive the recoding intact.
# Positions are derived from the SUPPLIED sequence, never typed in, so the
# check cannot drift if a part is replaced.
myg <- str_locate(mch_pep, "MYG")
stopifnot("No MYG chromophore tripeptide found in the supplied mCherry" =
            !is.na(myg[1]))

walk(builds, function(b) {
  mch_new <- b$parts$after[b$parts$part == "mCherry"]
  ff_new  <- b$parts$after[b$parts$part == "firefly luc2P"]
  ha_new  <- b$parts$after[b$parts$part == "HA (1x)"]
  stopifnot(
    "mCherry chromophore moved or was lost" =
      identical(str_locate(aa_of(mch_new), "MYG"), myg),
    "The recoded firefly lost the PEST degron" =
      endsWith(aa_of(ff_new), PEST_AA),
    "The recoded HA no longer encodes the epitope" = aa_of(ha_new) == HA_AA,
    "Recoded codons are not 231-like" =
      mean(USE[codon_split(paste0(mch_new, ff_new, ha_new))]) > 0.25
  )
})
cat(sprintf("Both orientations: mCherry MYG chromophore at residues %d-%d, firefly PEST intact, HA epitope intact\n",
            myg[1], myg[2]))
```

# 8. The Answer: Length and GC3

```{r composition}
part_tbl <- map_dfr(builds, function(b)
  b$parts %>%
    mutate(construct = b$label,
           nt = nchar(after), codons = nt / 3,
           gc3_before = map_dbl(before, compute_gc3_pct),
           gc3_after  = map_dbl(after,  compute_gc3_pct),
           gc_before  = map_dbl(before, gc_pct_of),
           gc_after   = map_dbl(after,  gc_pct_of)) %>%
    dplyr::select(construct, part, nt, codons, gc3_before, gc3_after,
                  gc_before, gc_after))

print(part_tbl %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>%
        as.data.frame())

comp_tbl <- map_dfr(builds, function(b) tibble(
  construct   = construct_names[[b$label]],
  orientation = b$label,
  nt_ordered  = nchar(b$full),
  cds_length  = nchar(b$sense),            # stop-free, the plotted basis
  protein_aa  = nchar(b$sense) / 3,
  gc3_before  = compute_gc3_pct(trim_internal(paste0(b$original_sense,
                                                     ORF_STOP))),
  gc3_pct     = compute_gc3_pct(trim_internal(b$full)),
  gc_pct      = gc_pct_of(b$sense)))

cat("\n=== Firefly transfection-efficiency control, both orientations ===\n")
print(comp_tbl %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>%
        as.data.frame())

# Joined, not compared positionally: `group_by()` returns groups in sorted
# order, which need not be build order. Here the two happen to coincide
# ("C-terminal" sorts before "N-terminal"), so a positional comparison passes
# by luck - rename either orientation and it would silently compare the wrong
# rows. `part_tbl`'s construct column holds the orientation label, so the join
# is on that.
part_sums <- part_tbl %>%
  group_by(construct) %>% summarise(part_nt = sum(nt), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::rename(orientation = construct)
len_check <- comp_tbl %>% left_join(part_sums, by = "orientation")

stopifnot(
  "A construct missed its GC3 target by more than 1 point" =
    all(abs(comp_tbl$gc3_pct - TARGET_GC3) <= 1),
  "An orientation is missing from the part table" =
    !any(is.na(len_check$part_nt)),
  "Part lengths do not sum to the construct length" =
    all(len_check$part_nt == len_check$cds_length)
)
cat(sprintf("\nGC3 target %.1f%%; both constructs within %.2f points.\n",
            TARGET_GC3, max(abs(comp_tbl$gc3_pct - TARGET_GC3))))
```

```{r percentiles}
ref_df  <- comp_tbl %>%
  transmute(reporter = construct, cds_length, gc_pct, gc3_pct)
pct_tbl <- reporter_percentiles(expressed, promoted, ref_df)
print(pct_tbl)
stopifnot("Percentiles must lie in [0, 100]" =
            all(between(pct_tbl$pct_expressed, 0, 100) &
                  between(pct_tbl$pct_promoted, 0, 100)))
```

# 9. Panels

Both constructs, nothing else on the figure.

**On the length panel the two lines coincide exactly**, since the orientations
are the same length. They are drawn solid and dashed so the second is not
hidden under the first - the same reason the helper carries a linetype column
at all.

```{r density_setup}
group_cols <- c("All expressed mRNAs"    = "grey70",
                "eIF3d hypoxia promotes" = "#E69F00")

# Okabe-Ito dark blue and reddish purple. Grey and orange are the two gene
# distributions, and the project reserves orange for eIF3d and sky blue for
# eIF3e, so neither can be used for a construct without the line reading as a
# factor.
ref_plot_df <- ref_df %>%
  mutate(color    = c("#0072B2", "#CC79A7"),
         linetype = c("solid", "dashed"),
         reporter = factor(reporter, levels = reporter))
```

```{r panel_length, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=5.5}
p_len <- plot_density_luc(
  expressed, promoted, "cds_length",
  xlab    = "CDS length (kb)",
  title   = "CDS length, MDA-MB-231, firefly/mCherry P2A controls",
  outfile = "cds_reporter_14_density_cds_length.pdf",
  luc_tbl = ref_plot_df, group_cols = group_cols,
  xscale  = 1000, xmax = params$xmax_kb)
```

```{r panel_gc3, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=5.5}
p_gc3 <- plot_density_luc(
  expressed, promoted, "gc3_pct",
  xlab    = "CDS GC3 content (%)",
  title   = "CDS GC3 content, MDA-MB-231, firefly/mCherry P2A controls",
  outfile = "cds_reporter_14_density_cds_gc3.pdf",
  luc_tbl = ref_plot_df, group_cols = group_cols)
```

# 10. Outputs

```{r write_outputs}
outdir <- here("output", "cds_reporter_design")

# One row per construct, with the recoded parts in a column named for the part
# rather than by position: the two orientations hold the same five parts in a
# different order, so `part1`/`part4` columns would mean different things in
# the two rows and could not be read down the column.
#
# `cds` is the full ordered ORF including the terminal stop - these constructs
# terminate, unlike `08_`/`12_`, so there is no separate stop-free column to
# synthesise from.
seq_tbl <- map_dfr(builds, function(b) {
  parts_wide <- set_names(as.list(b$parts$after),
                          c("mcherry", "ha", "gs_linker", "p2a",
                            "firefly")[match(b$parts$part,
                                             c("mCherry", "HA (1x)", GS_PART,
                                               P2A_PART, "firefly luc2P"))])
  tibble(construct   = construct_names[[b$label]],
         orientation = b$label,
         layout      = paste(b$parts$part, collapse = " - "),
         nt_ordered  = nchar(b$full),
         nt_stopfree = nchar(b$sense),
         protein_aa  = nchar(b$sense) / 3,
         stop_codon  = ORF_STOP,
         !!!parts_wide,
         cds         = b$full)
}) %>%
  left_join(comp_tbl %>% dplyr::select(construct, gc3_pct, gc3_before, gc_pct),
            by = "construct")
stopifnot(
  "A part column is missing from the exported sequence table" =
    all(c("mcherry", "ha", "gs_linker", "p2a", "firefly") %in% names(seq_tbl))
)

write_csv(seq_tbl, file.path(outdir, "14_p2a_controls_sequences.csv"))
write_csv(part_tbl, file.path(outdir, "14_p2a_controls_part_composition.csv"))
write_csv(comp_tbl, file.path(outdir, "14_p2a_controls_composition.csv"))
write_csv(pct_tbl,  file.path(outdir, "14_p2a_controls_percentiles_vs_231.csv"))

cat("Wrote 4 tables to", outdir, "\n")
```
